question.leadin: Give the following about Belgian involvement in World War II.
question.text: The invasion of Belgium by German forces was part of their plan to bypass this series of fortifications on the Franco-German border.
question.clue: Army Group C conducted a holding action at this place, which allowed Army Groups A and B to move north and then west in the sickle-slice maneuver.

swap.leadin: The Treaty of Verdun divided this man's lands between Lothair, Charles the Bald, and Louis the German.
swap.text: Name this son of Pepin the Short, a Frankish king who conquered much of Western Europe.
swap.answerHtml: Charlemagne [or Charles I or Charles the Great; or Carolus Magnus; prompt on Charles]
swap.clue: After the Battle of Fontenoy, this man's grandchildren split his empire into three parts in the Treaty of Verdun.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about a student protest.
question.text: In 1968, student protesters in this city clashed with police in the Latin Quarter. A massive strike ensued, and Jacques Chirac was sent to negotiate with workers.
question.clue: Defense Minister Leon Gambetta fled this city in a hot air balloon the year before a revolutionary regime in this city was ousted during the "Bloody Week."

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about Muslim Spain.
swap.text: This first Carolingian emperor, whose eponym means "hammer", prevented the Umayyads from moving from Spain into France at the 732 Battle of Tours.
swap.clue: He served as Mayor of the Palace in Austrasia, a title he passed to his son, Pepin III after securing another victory at the Battle of Cologne.

question.leadin: This saint was burned at the stake after being captured by English forces.
question.text: Name this French saint, a peasant girl who believed that God told her to drive out the English.
question.clue: Guillaume de Flavy stranded this figure outside the gates of Compeigne by lifting a drawbridge too soon, allowing John of Luxembourg to capture this leader, who was then subjected to a trial led by Bishop Pierre Cauchon.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the Sun King.
swap.text: One of Louis's most expensive projects was this royal palace and garden complex that is located southwest of Paris.
swap.clue: Charles Le Brun painted much of the ceiling and arches of the largest room in this location, which is stocked with an enormous amount of mirrors.

question.text: During the Seventh Crusade, Shajar al-Durr's forces captured this French king and held him for ransom. This king later died in Tunisia during the Eighth Crusade.
question.clue: This man's exploits were chronicled by Jean de Joinville.

swap.text: This clergyman succeeded Richelieu as chief minister of France and was an important adviser to Anne of Austria, regent during Louis's youth.
swap.clue: This protege of Cardinal Richelieu served as Louis XIV's chief minister. He defeated anti-monarchical forces during the Fronde Rebellion and later negotiated the Peace of the Pyrenees.

question.text: A king of this name, known as the Quarreller, ruled Navarre in the early fourteenth Century. Kings of this name from another country include ones known as "The Fat" and "The German."
question.clue: The Albigensian Crusade ended during Blanche of Castile's Regency for another king of this name, who was canonized after leading the Seventh and Eighth Crusades.

swap.text: Robespierre clashed with this president of the Committee of Public Safety, whose attempts to moderate the Reign of Terror only provoked his own guillotining.
swap.clue: This man founded an organization to prevent the "infractions of the rights of man" known as the Cordeliers Club.

question.text: The Popular Front organized the Million Franc Race to encourage competition with German automobile manufacturers, which was eventually won by a man with this last name. A man with this last name was opposed by La Libre Parole and imprisoned on Devil's Island.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the foremost legal battle of the French Third Republic.
swap.text: This French socialist leader and cofounder of the newspaper L'Humanite campaigned hard for Revision with his book Les Preuves; backlash from it cost him his seat in the Chamber of Deputies.
swap.answer: Auguste Marie Joseph Jean Leon Jaures
swap.clue: The Socialist Party which Blum joined had been founded in 1905 from a disparate coalition of splinter groups by this cofounder of the newspaper L'Humanite, who in 1914 was assassinated for his pacifism.

question.leadin: It called for the cession of the Austrian Netherlands to and the recognition of the Cisalpine and.
question.text: Name this peace treaty signed between and on Oct. 17, 1797, ending Napoleon's war in .
question.clue: The subsequent Treaty of Luneville required the enforcement of this treaty, which was signed just a month after the Coup of 18 Fructidor.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about European Wars of Religion.
swap.text: This religiously motivated civil war in France was fought between factions supporting the claims of three men of the same name to the French throne.
swap.clue: Another figure in this conflict was Alexander Farnese, the Duke of Parma, whose command undid one side's losses at Arques and Ivry and broke the eventual victor's siege of Rouen.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the report of the Bergier commission, a panel of historians who investigated the actions of Switzerland before, during, and after World War II.
question.text: The report stated that Swiss participation at a conference on Jewish refugees held in this French town aimed to take in as few refugees as possible. This town also names a treaty that ended the Algerian War of Independence.
question.clue: FDR convened a 1938 conference in this city to address the status of stateless Jewish refugees. A set of peace treaties signed in this city addressed the refugee statuses of the Harki and a group whose name means "black feet."

swap.leadin: Name these saints associated with the French monarchy.
swap.text: This third-century Martyr is the patron saint of France and supposedly walked several miles carrying his severed head. Abbot Suger helped build his namesake cathedral north of Paris, which housed the Oriflamme.

question.leadin: A gilt eagle named for this person is mounted on a vase and displayed in the Louvre alongside the French crown jewels.
question.text: Name this royal advisor who was convinced by Bernard of Clairvaux's Apologia to devote himself to religious life. He later unsuccessfully lobbied Louis VII not to join the Second Crusade.
question.answerHtml: Abbot Suger (“soo-zhair”) [or Abbé Suger; or Sugerius; accept Suger’s Eagle or Aigle du Suger]
question.clue: Much of our knowledge of Louis comes from the writings of this abbot of St. Denis, who was Louis's advisor; he would later serve as Louis 's regent during the Second Crusade.

swap.text: This month had days named after exciting things like crabs, barleygrass, buckhorn, puffball, licorice, and horse chestnuts. The twelfth month of the French Revolutionary Calendar, it preceded the Sansculottides and on the 18th of this month, in 1799, General Augeau purged 130 members of the Directory.

question.text: This ex-Huguenot leader allied with Jenatsch to kick Habsburg forces out of the Valtellina valley. His brother of the same surname, the Duke of Soubise, tried to defend La Rochelle during the 1627 siege.
question.answerHtml: Henri de Rohan [accept the Duc de Rohan or Duke of Rohan]

swap.leadin: A biography of this ruler by Samuel Putnam describes her as the "first modern woman."
swap.text: Name this author and patron who protected Francois Rabelais and have influenced Anne Boleyn's conversion to Protestantism during the latter's service to her sister-in-law Queen Claude. She negotiated her brother Francis I's release after his capture at the Battle of Pavia.
swap.answerHtml: Marguerite of Navarre [or Marguerite of Angoulême; accept Margaret for “Marguerite”]
